descriptionChirho: Baldness or a bald patch (קָרְחָה), predominantly used in the context of mourning rites and their prohibition: shaving the head as a sign of grief or cultic practice (Dt 14:1; Isa 3:24; 15:2; 22:12; Jer 47:5; 48:37; Ezek 7:18; 27:31; Amos 8:10; Mic 1:16). The term appears in both forbidden mourning customs ('do not make baldness between your eyes') and descriptive lament contexts. All three clusters are grammatical inflections: absolute noun, with 2fs suffix ('your baldness'), and with preposition lamed plus conjunction. Arabic renders 'صَلَعٌ/قَرْعَة,' Korean '대머리,' Swahili 'upara/kipara,' Spanish 'calvicie/calvas,' and Hindi 'गंजापन/गंजा,' all pointing to the same concept of ritual head-shaving or baldness.
